sections.html:
Nashua is a city in southern New Hampshire on the Massachusetts line, in southeastern Hillsborough County. It shares the county seat role with Manchester. The 2020 count was 91,322 residents, and there were 39,663 housing units, 3.6 percent of them vacant. The Merrimack River forms the eastern boundary and the Nashua River roughly cuts the city in two.

Buyers and sellers use neighborhood names more than the official ward map:

  • Downtown, centered on Main Street and the Nashua River
  • French Hill in the north
  • The Tree Streets neighborhood near downtown
  • The Amherst Street corridor (Route 101A) in the northwest
  • South Nashua along Daniel Webster Highway, next to the state line

The mills ran from the 1820s until the last one near Nashua closed in 1949. The city's recovery began when Sanders Associates, now part of BAE Systems, moved into a closed mill, and Digital Equipment Corporation arrived in the 1970s. Housing today reflects both the mill era and the later technology decades. The buyer pool includes commuters to the Boston area, who use the Everett Turnpike and a bus line out of the Nashua Transit Center at Exit 8.

Nashua winters are real. Normals show about 52.9 inches of snow and 48.19 inches of precipitation a year, with a January daily mean of 24.1 degrees Fahrenheit. The city also averages 26 to 30 days a year at 90 degrees or above. With that much snow and rain, the roof, gutters and basement are the first things to check before you list, or the first things a cash buyer will price in.

The Assessing Department sets values and the Tax Collector's Office bills and collects the tax. Both are at City Hall, 229 Main Street, Nashua, NH 03060.

OfficePhoneNotes
Assessing Department603-589-3040Abatement desk open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., closed 12:30 to 1:30 p.m.
Tax Collector603-589-3190Mail to P.O. Box 885, Nashua, NH 03061

A mailed payment is on time if it is postmarked by the due date. You can also pay through the city's Pay Bills Online portal, by phone at 1-833-343-0229, at the counter, or in the secure drop box at the Elm Street entrance of City Hall. Accepted forms are cash, major credit cards, checks, money orders and bank checks. Starting with the first 2026 bills, taxpayers can view and download bills, payment history and balances online at any time.

Nashua's tax year runs April 1 to March 31, with two bills. The first is due July 1 and is an estimate based on 50 percent of the prior year's rate. The second is due after the state sets the rate, generally no later than December 20. When a home is bought or sold, property taxes are prorated by day from April 1. Late payments carry 8 percent interest, which matches RSA 76:13.

Recent rates per $1,000 of value show why a lower rate does not always mean a lower bill. In 2023 the rate was $18.23. In 2024 it was $15.90, down 12.8 percent, while total value rose from $13.9 billion to $16.5 billion (18.7 percent). In 2025 it was $16.83, up 5.83 percent. Check the city's Tax Rate History page for the figure that applies to your bill.

File a printed, signed application with the Assessing Department by March 1 after the notice of tax. The city accepts applications only after the final notice of tax is issued. If you miss March 1, no action can be taken for the current tax year, although you can ask for a spring review for the following year.

The fillable online form does not submit anywhere. Print it, sign it, keep a copy, and hand-deliver it to 229 Main Street or mail it to P.O. Box 2019, Nashua, NH 03061. Appeals beyond the city go to the New Hampshire Board of Tax and Land Appeals.

If your name or address is wrong on the bill, make the request in writing, signed by the owners, then fax it to 603-589-3079 or mail it to the Assessing Department. The Tax Collector cannot change it.

sections.h2: If you sell and still get the bill
sections.html:
Forward the bill to the new owner, or send it back in the provided envelope with a note saying when you sold and to whom. A deed can take time to reach the Assessor, which is why bills sometimes arrive in the old owner's name.

Unpaid tax can become a lien under the state's collection law. RSA 80:69 sets interest at 14 percent per year on a recorded real estate tax lien, and the lien can be redeemed at any time before the collector gives a deed.

  • Closing agents can request a final wastewater bill for a sale closing through a form on the city's Tax and Wastewater page.
  • Look up the account by its 8-digit parcel ID, found in the upper right corner of the bill.
  • The state transfer tax is $0.75 per $100 of the price, paid by both buyer and seller.

faqs.q: When are Nashua property tax bills due?
faqs.a: The first bill is due July 1 and the second is generally due no later than December 20.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to apply for a Nashua abatement?
faqs.a: March 1 after the notice of tax. Miss it and the city takes no action for that tax year, though you may ask for a spring review for the following year.

faqs.q: Are Nashua property taxes prorated when a house sells?
faqs.a: Yes. Taxes are prorated by day from April 1 of that year when a home is bought or sold.

faqs.q: What interest does Nashua charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: 8 percent. Mailed payments must be postmarked by the due date to avoid that interest charge.

faqs.q: Which county does Nashua's deed go to?
faqs.a: Hillsborough County. Deeds are recorded with the Hillsborough County Register of Deeds, and the transfer tax stamps are bought there, at $0.75 per $100 from each side.
